finding: The PII gate failed OPEN: with no --task and no --pii the launcher routed the invocation to the free provider. It now fails CLOSED. While the route is anything but subscription, an invocation reaches a free provider only when its --task name is on the free-OK allow-list or it carries an explicit --no-pii; everything else — no task, an unknown task, an interactive session — is deferred (exit 75) or pinned to the local model.
evidence: Harness: stub `claude`, throwaway HOME, subscription genuinely limited (stub returns the limit JSON), a live stand-in /healthz on 127.0.0.1:20999 so the gate is actually reached (with the port dead both versions defer on 'OmniRoute unhealthy' before the gate, which is why the first battery was inconclusive). BEFORE `claude-auto --force free -p hello`: exit=1, log 'route=free-fallback model=auto/coding:free task=? pii=0 headless=1', stub saw 'ARGS=-p hello | BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20999 | AUTH_TOKEN=set | MODEL=auto/coding:free | ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0'. AFTER: exit=75, stderr 'not cleared for a free provider — no --task and no --no-pii: fail closed', log 'defer task=none pii=1 (no --task and no --no-pii: fail closed)', the stub saw nothing. Same for the interactive shape `--force free --remote-control Vanessa --agent vanessa-orchestrator`: before it opened the session on the free route (headless=0), after exit=75.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh: is_pii=1 is the default; the classification block (`is_pii=1; why=...`) only lowers it for an allow-listed task or an explicit --no-pii that no client-data pattern objects to. The reason is printed on stderr and logged as `task=… pii=… (why)` on every route decision.

finding: Option parsing broke at the first non-option argument, so `-p hello --task lofty-crm-sync` never saw the task name and routed a client task to the free provider — and passed `--task lofty-crm-sync` on to claude as its own arguments. All options are now recognised in any position before `--`; every other argument goes to claude untouched in its original order.
evidence: BEFORE `claude-auto --force free -p hello --task lofty-crm-sync`: exit=1, log 'task=? pii=0', stub saw 'ARGS=-p hello --task lofty-crm-sync | BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20999 | ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0'. AFTER: exit=75, log 'defer task=lofty-crm-sync pii=1 (task matches client-data pattern 'lofty-*')' — byte-identical outcome to the `--task`-first ordering. `--task=NAME` also works (log 'task allow-listed by 'mortgage-rates-daily''). F-V2-16 in passing: `claude-auto --task` → 'claude-auto: --task needs a value' + usage, exit 64 (was a raw '$2: unbound variable', exit 1).
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh option loop: --task/--task=/--force/--force=/--pii/--no-pii/--status collected wherever they appear, CARGS carries the rest, `--` ends option parsing; a task name is charset-checked ([A-Za-z0-9_.-]).

finding: PII matching was exact-name against a hard-coded list, so any renamed or new client task fell through to the free provider. Replaced with an ALLOW-LIST of tasks permitted on free providers (glob patterns, DEFAULT_FREE_OK_TASKS + ~/.config/omniroute/free-ok-tasks.txt) plus a pattern DENY-LIST (DEFAULT_PII_TASKS + pii-tasks.txt) that wins over the allow-list and over --no-pii. Chosen because a deny-list fails open on every name nobody has classified yet, while an allow-list fails closed; the deny-list stays as belt-and-braces so a client task can never be allow-listed by mistake.
evidence: BEFORE, OmniRoute answering: `--task lofty-crm-sync-v2`, `--task some-brand-new-task`, `--task nightly-borrower-export` and `--task lofty-crm-sync --no-pii` all reached the stub on the free route ('ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0'). AFTER: exit=75 each, with the reason — "matches client-data pattern 'lofty-*'", "task not on the free-OK allow-list: fail closed", "matches client-data pattern '*borrower*'", "matches client-data pattern 'lofty-*' (--no-pii refused)". free-ok-tasks.txt with `brain-deck-sync` and `feeds-*`: `--task brain-deck-sync` and `--task feeds-hourly` routed free ('task allow-listed by 'feeds-*''), `--task feeds-crm-export` still deferred ('matches client-data pattern '*crm*''). Every name in the old exact list is covered by a pattern (lofty-*, zoho-*, isa-*, lead-*, r12-inbox-*, r13-appointment-*, showing-*, steve-twin-*, r11-isa-* via *-isa-*, vanessa-imessage/discord/whatsapp-*, health-*).
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh DEFAULT_FREE_OK_TASKS (11 names whose inputs are public or system data per their doc names: weather/news/rates/market feeds/model feeds/incentives/skills/feed freshness/runner health/toolkit) and DEFAULT_PII_TASKS (41 patterns). `set -f` so the patterns are never expanded against the cwd. Pattern files: comments and blanks stripped, charset-checked.

finding: The usage-limit regex read the task's whole stdout+stderr and its `[^0-9]429[^0-9]`, `resets? (at|in)` and `limit (has been )?reached` branches matched ordinary mortgage prose, flipping a healthy subscription onto a free model whenever a run also failed. Now (1) the regex only ever sees the ERROR ENVELOPE — in JSON mode the result/error/message/subtype fields of the {"type":"result"} object; in text mode stderr plus the last three stdout lines, and only when the exit code is non-zero — and (2) the vocabulary is anchored: taken from the strings inside the Claude Code 2.1.278 binary (`usage limit`, `you've hit your … limit`, `rate_limit_error`, `rate limited`), with 429 only next to API Error/HTTP/status/code or 'Too Many Requests', and no bare resets/limit-reached branches.
evidence: Unit test of LIMIT_RE, before → after: 'Loan amount $429,000 on the subject property' MATCH → no; 'Comp at 429, Elm Street' MATCH → no; 'HTTP 200 OK, 429 ms elapsed' MATCH → no; 'Property tax resets at the start of the fiscal year' MATCH → no; 'The escrow limit has been reached for this account' MATCH → no; 'Index 429 of 5000 rows processed' MATCH → no. Non-limits stay unmatched in both: 'API Error: 401 Invalid API key · Please run /login', 'Fast mode overloaded…', 'API Error: 529 overloaded_error'. Real shapes all MATCH after: 'Claude AI usage limit reached|<epoch>', "You've hit your limit · resets 3pm", 'You’ve hit your weekly limit' (curly apostrophe), 'Usage limit reached · continuing automatically', 'API Error: 429 {…rate_limit_error…}', '"error": {"type": "rate_limit_error"…}', 'the request was rate limited' (missed before), "You're out of extra usage", 'HTTP 429 Too Many Requests'. End-to-end on the subscription path: a task exiting 1 with the six prose lines in its output — BEFORE 'LIMIT detected … -> mode=free-fallback', exit 75; AFTER 'run failed task=weather-news-refresh rc=1 — not a usage limit, route unchanged', exit 1, mode stays subscription. A real limit still switches: JSON legacy form → 'branch=usage-limit', text form → 'branch=hit-your-limit', 429 body on stderr → 'branch=rate_limit-token', each exit 75 and mode=free-fallback; the 401 login-expiry does not switch.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh LIMIT_RE, envelope(), limit_branch(); probe.sh carries the identical LIMIT_RE and envelope_text() (checked equal in the test). README 'The detection signal' rewritten to match.

finding: A probe that failed for any reason other than a limit match kept the free-fallback mode forever, and the launcher swallowed its own re-probe with `|| true`. Now the probe counts consecutive inconclusive runs in state/probe-failures; at OMNIROUTE_PROBE_MAX_FAIL (default 4 = one hour) it writes state/NEEDS-STEVEN (what failed, what to check), falls the route back to plain `claude` (mode=subscription — the one route that cannot leak, and a still-limited subscription simply re-flips on the next headless run), logs ESCALATED and exits 1. Any conclusive probe resets the counter and clears the marker. The launcher logs the exit status of its self-probe, and writes the marker if probe.sh is missing next to it (F-V2-17).
evidence: BEFORE: five probe.sh runs with a `claude` stub exiting 2 → each 'probe inconclusive (rc=2) — mode kept: free-fallback', mode free-fallback after all five, no counter, no marker; launcher log in the same state showed only the defer line — nothing about the failed probe. AFTER: '1/4', '2/4', '3/4', then at the 4th 'ESCALATED: 4 consecutive inconclusive probes (rc=2) — mode=subscription (fail back to plain claude), marker written at …/state/NEEDS-STEVEN', probe-failures reset to 0, exit 1; the 5th run exits 0 (subscription mode). Marker text: 'probe.sh: 4 consecutive inconclusive probes (last rc=2) — switch-back cannot be proven, so the route fell back to plain claude … Check that claude is on the LaunchAgent PATH, that its -p flags still exist, and that it is logged in … Delete this file once fixed.' Launcher with the same broken stub: log 'self-probe rc=1 (state was >1500s old)'. Launcher copied without probe.sh: log 'ERROR probe.sh not found or not executable at …/alone/probe.sh' and marker 'claude-auto: probe.sh missing at … — switch-back is impossible until it is installed next to claude-auto'. Legitimate switch-back unchanged: free-fallback + healthy stub → 'RESTORED: subscription usable again', route.env mode=subscription; still-limited → 'still limited: mode=free-fallback reset_at=… branch=usage-limit'. mac-verify.sh reports the marker as NEED (F-H3-16).
fix: DONE. probe.sh: FAILS counter, fail_count(), escalation block, marker clearing on RESTORED; claude-auto.sh: symlink-resolved probe path, `prc=$?` logged, write_marker on a missing probe.

finding: A reset epoch parsed from a limit message was stored verbatim; a far-future value silenced the probe forever. Now the epoch is taken only from the CLI's own `limit reached|<10 digits>` shape (anchored with `[|]`, so a pipe-delimited table cell no longer parses) and clamped to now−1h..now+48h (OMNIROUTE_RESET_MAX_AHEAD); anything outside is a parse failure → 0 → the probe polls. The clamp is applied again when route.env is read, so a bad value already on disk is neutralised too, and the probe re-probes at least every 6 h (OMNIROUTE_PROBE_FORCE_AGE) regardless of reset_at.
evidence: BEFORE: route.env seeded with reset_at=4102444800, LaunchAgent-style `probe.sh` (no --now) → log 'waiting: mode=free-fallback reset_at=4102444800', exit 0, no probe, mode stays free-fallback; a limit message carrying |4102444800 → route.env reset_at=4102444800. AFTER: same seed → 'WARN reset_at=4102444800 in …/route.env is outside the sane window — treated as 0 (probe now)' then 'RESTORED: subscription usable again'; the limit message → 'reset epoch 4102444800 is outside now-1h..now+172800s — treated as unknown (0)', route.env reset_at=0; a sane epoch 30 min out is kept (reset_at=1790092100). Note the CLI itself carries the string 'the usage limit now resets more than 24 hours out, so this task will not resume on its own' — a real reset can be days out; a clamped value costs nothing because a limited probe fails fast.
fix: DONE. parse_reset_epoch() and the read_route() clamp in both scripts; PROBE_FORCE_AGE in probe.sh (wait branch) and claude-auto.sh (stale test).

finding: The .env mode check used BSD-first `stat -f %Lp || stat -c %a`; on Linux `stat -f` succeeds with a filesystem report, so the whole free-route path exited 78 on any Linux host. Replaced with mac-verify.sh's filemode() (GNU first, validated as octal, BSD fallback) and a fileowner() twin used by the route.env trust check.
evidence: Raw pre-fix script on this Linux host, .env genuinely -rw-------, OmniRoute answering: exit=78, stderr 'must be chmod 600 (is   File: "…/.env"  ID: … Type: ext2/ext3 Block size: 4096 …'. AFTER: the same invocation passes the check and the allow-listed task reaches the stub on the free route; with the file deliberately chmod 644: exit=78, 'must be chmod 600 (is 644)'. (For the other before/after batteries the pre-fix script ran behind a `stat` shim that fails `stat -f`, the only way to get it past this bug to its gate; the after runs used the real GNU stat.) README's 'stat -f … macOS forms with GNU fallbacks' claim corrected.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh filemode()/fileowner() (same shape as mac-verify.sh:47-55), used in load_omni_key() and route_file_trusted(); probe.sh carries the same two functions.

finding: redact() only caught `(sk|key|token|Bearer)[-_ ]…`, so NAME=value, name: value, JSON "api_key":"value", x-api-key: value, CLI `--api-key value` and quoted values passed through. claude-auto.sh no longer has a redact() at all because it no longer writes any output text to disk (F-H3-09). probe.sh's redact() (its 200-byte inconclusive-probe sample) and a new redact_line() in mac-verify.sh (everything echoed from another tool's listing) now apply four ordered rules: identifier containing key/token/secret/pass/auth/cred + = or : (+ optional Bearer/Basic/Token scheme word) + value, in single or double quotes or bare; the same words + whitespace/dash + an 8+ char run (the CLI-flag form); bare sk-/Bearer/ghp_/xox tokens; any 32+ char opaque run. Case-insensitive via bracket classes because BSD sed has no I flag.
evidence: Ten obvious fake placeholders of the form FAKE-PLACEHOLDER-00NN in the shapes NAME=v, 'Invalid token: v', {"api_key":"v"}, 'x-api-key: v', NAME=sk-ant-v, 'Authorization: Bearer v', 'password = v', "client_secret": "v", '--api-key v - ✓ Connected', export NAME='v'. BEFORE (probe.sh:16 one-liner): 6 of 8 survived. AFTER: 0 of 10 survive through probe.sh redact and 0 of 10 through mac-verify redact_line; a harmless line ('usage limit reached|1790000000 rc=1 … API Error: 429 rate_limit_error') passes untouched. Two of my own first-draft rules leaked in testing and were fixed before hand-back: the Bearer scheme word was being consumed as the value, and a single-quoted value was skipped.
fix: DONE. probe.sh redact(); mac-verify.sh redact_line(); the two are kept textually in step (comment in each).

finding: limit-samples.log appended up to 300 bytes of the failing task's own stdout+stderr — the tasks most likely to fail being the client-data ones — into a world-readable file in a default-umask directory. Now: `umask 077` in both scripts, state/ chmod 700, every file 600; on a detected limit the launcher records timestamp, task, exit status, pii flag, which regex branch fired, byte count and the sha256 of the envelope — never the text; the file is capped at 500 lines (the run logs at 5000). The probe's inconclusive samples keep a redacted 200-byte head because the probe's prompt is fixed text.
evidence: BEFORE, real limit on the subscription path: limit-samples.log line '… task=weather-news-refresh rc=1 sample={"type":"result","subtype":"error_during_execution","is_error":true,"result":"Claude AI usage limit reached|…",…}' (the whole output), state dir drwxr-xr-x, limit-samples.log and route.env -rw-r--r--. AFTER: '… task=weather-news-refresh rc=1 pii=0 branch=usage-limit bytes=86 sha256=9c7f465443bad8f88fad2f9f684dff4b19a52360f09ace859f49662c83a27757', state dir drwx------, both files -rw-------. Probe inconclusive line: '… probe rc=2 inconclusive=1/4 bytes=33 sha256=… sample=error: unknown option --max-turns'.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh record_sample()/hash256()/rotate(), umask 077 + chmod 700; probe.sh the same plus redact() on its own sample. The README's original 'tighten LIMIT_RE from the samples' purpose is now served by the branch label, not by stored text.

finding: route.env was SOURCED on every invocation from a default-umask directory whose mode was never checked. It is now a data file: the six keys are read with sed and validated (mode must be one of three words, numbers must be digits, reason charset-limited, omni_ok 0/1), never sourced; a route.env that is not a plain file owned by the user with mode 600/400 has its content discarded and is rewritten as mode=subscription (rather than merely skipped, which would have re-trusted the planted content once the mode was fixed).
evidence: Injection, route.env containing `mode=subscription; touch /tmp/h3-test/PWNED-<run>` at mode 600: BEFORE the PWNED file was created (the line executed) and the run went on normally; AFTER no PWNED file, and the launcher refused with "unknown mode 'subscription_ touch …' in …/route.env" exit 78 (the sanitiser turns `;` into `_`). World-writable route.env (666) saying free-fallback, OmniRoute answering: BEFORE trusted → task ran on the free route ('ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0'); AFTER 'WARN …/route.env is not a plain owner-only file (mode 666, owner 0) — content discarded, route reset to subscription', route.env recreated -rw------- with reason='untrusted-route-file-reset', the stub saw ROUTE=subscription, and a second run found nothing planted.
fix: DONE. route_get()/route_num()/route_file_trusted()/read_route() in both scripts; write_route unchanged apart from the wider sanitiser set.

finding: Fixed in passing while rewriting the option loop and the self-probe block: `--task`/`--force` as the last argument now produce the script's own usage message (exit 64) instead of a `set -u` crash; the probe is located through a symlink-resolving loop (bash 3.2 has no `readlink -f`) and its absence is logged and marked instead of being indistinguishable from an inconclusive probe.
evidence: `claude-auto --task` → 'claude-auto: --task needs a value' + usage line, exit 64 (before: 'line 38: $2: unbound variable', exit 1). Launcher in a directory without probe.sh: log 'ERROR probe.sh not found or not executable at …' + NEEDS-STEVEN marker (before: `>/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, nothing).
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh usage_err(), option loop guards, `self=$0` readlink loop.

finding: The README's PII canary only exercised the one ordering that already passed. It now has 11 steps: client task with options first; the same with --task AFTER the claude arguments; no --task; a renamed client task; an unclassified task; --no-pii on a client task (deny-list must win); an interactive session with no task — all seven must exit 75 with zero requests at :20128; an allow-listed task and a --no-pii session must come from OmniRoute; an allow-listed task whose PROMPT drags in the canary file is the existing guard hook's test (the launcher sees names, not prompt text); then --force subscription. It also says to unload the probe LaunchAgent for the duration, because a healthy probe would restore the subscription mid-canary.
evidence: README.md 'PII canary' section; each step was run in the sandbox harness with the expected result (F-H3-01..03 evidence, plus the canary-scenario run on a healthy stub: steps 2 and 3 exit 75, step 8 and 9 reach the stub with 'BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20999 | ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0', step 11 restores 'ROUTE=subscription | PII_OK=1').
fix: DONE in the README. The acceptance run itself is on the Mac, with the security steward, and records into docs/MASTER-FINDINGS.md under F-E8-60 — Steven's, not mine.

finding: integrations/CONNECTIONS.md:45 claimed 'Client-data tasks defer (exit 75) while on free providers' next to 'syntax-checked, not executed'. Reworded to what is now true and how it was established.
evidence: CONNECTIONS.md:45 now reads: 'Scripts executed in the sandbox (H3, 2026-09-22) against a stub `claude`, a dead `:20128` and a live stand-in `/healthz`, not on the Mac. The PII gate now fails closed: while on free providers every invocation defers (exit 75) unless its `--task` name is on the free-OK allow-list or it carries an explicit `--no-pii`, in any argument order; client-data name patterns (…) win over both. F-V2-07/08/09/10/11/12/13/14/15/18 fixed; the switch-back probe escalates to `state/NEEDS-STEVEN` after four inconclusive runs instead of stranding.' The rest of the row (HALT items, trust level L1) is untouched.
fix: DONE.

finding: The vendored-skills check only tested that SKILL.md existed. It now parses each skill's frontmatter (the block between the two --- fences, via awk), requires name == directory name and a non-empty description (block scalars handled), and resolves every relative ](link) in the body; each failure is a FAIL for that skill, and the nine become nine lines.
evidence: Fake repo with security-and-hardening/SKILL.md replaced by V2's broken version (`name: TOTALLY-WRONG-NAME`, unterminated flow sequence) and a dead link appended to find-skills/SKILL.md. BEFORE: 'ok    vendored skills            all nine present'. AFTER: "FAIL  skill security-and-hardening frontmatter name 'TOTALLY-WRONG-NAME' is not the directory name — the loader rejects it", 'FAIL  skill find-skills          dead relative link(s): ../../references/does-not-exist.md', and for the seven intact skills 'ok    skill <name>  loads: name matches, description NNN chars, links resolve' (237–425 chars, matching V2's PyYAML measurement). Backticked paths are not resolved (ambiguous with commands) — only ](…) links; stated here so nobody assumes more.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh skills block. Read-only: it only reads the nine files.

finding: An installed claude-auto or probe.sh that differed from the repo copy was reported ok with an advisory. It is now NEED (lands in the summary, blocks exit 0); a missing repo copy is FAIL.
evidence: Fake HOME with a two-line 'echo TAMPERED' at ~/.local/bin/claude-auto. BEFORE: 'ok    claude-auto                installed (differs from the repo copy — diff it before trusting it)'. AFTER: 'NEED  claude-auto                installed copy DIFFERS from the repo copy — diff it, then reinstall from the repo before trusting the gate', listed under NEEDS STEVEN, exit 1.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh omniroute block.

finding: A route mode other than subscription was reported ok. It is now NEED with the age computed from route.env's since= (parsed with sed, never sourced) and the recorded reason; the NEEDS-STEVEN escalation marker is a NEED of its own and a non-zero probe-failures counter is reported as info.
evidence: State seeded to free-fallback with since 3h07m ago and a marker. BEFORE: 'ok    omniroute route mode       free-fallback'. AFTER: 'NEED  omniroute route mode       free-fallback for 3h7m (reason: limit-detected task=weather-news-refresh) — the probe has not restored the subscription' and 'NEED  omniroute probe            ESCALATED — 2026-09-22T14:00:00Z probe.sh: 4 consecutive inconclusive probes (last rc=2)  switch-back cannot be proven'.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh OMNI_STATE block.

finding: check_cmd reported ok with a blank version for a binary that failed to run. It now tests the exit status and the output: non-zero → FAIL 'exited N', empty → FAIL 'printed nothing'.
evidence: Stubs on PATH: graphify exits 1, codeburn exits 0 printing nothing, headroom prints a version. BEFORE: 'ok    codeburn' and 'ok    graphify' with empty version fields. AFTER: "FAIL  graphify                   on PATH at …/bin/graphify but 'graphify --version' exited 1", "FAIL  codeburn                   on PATH at …/bin/codeburn but 'codeburn --version' printed nothing", 'ok    headroom                   headroom 0.38.0'.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh check_cmd().

finding: The MCP check merged stderr, ignored the exit status and counted lines. It now reads stdout only and tests the exit status (a failure re-reads stderr with a second, identical read-only call and reports its first line, redacted), treats 'No MCP servers configured' as NEED, counts server lines (`name: …`) rather than lines, flags servers marked ✗/Failed to connect as NEED, and pipes the printed listing through redact_line(). That last part closed a gap V2 did not list: the old script printed a server's full command line, so an inline `--api-key VALUE` would have reached the report.
evidence: Stub `claude mcp list` in three cases. Empty state — BEFORE 'ok    claude mcp list            1 line(s) returned'; AFTER 'NEED  claude mcp list            no MCP servers configured for this user — the brain's local servers are not registered'. Exit 1 with 'Error: config unreadable' on stderr — AFTER 'FAIL  claude mcp list            exited 1 — Error: config unreadable'. Three servers, one failing, one with `--api-key FAKE-PLACEHOLDER-MCP-0001` on its command line — AFTER 'ok    claude mcp list            3 server(s) listed', 'NEED  MCP servers failing        1 server(s) not connected — see the listing', listing line 'perplexity: node /x/server.js --api-key [REDACTED] - ✓ Connected'; grep of the report for MCP-0001: 0 (my first redact_line printed it — fixed before hand-back). The agent402 refusal check is kept.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh MCP block + redact_line().

finding: A placeholder credential passed as set. The value is now read into a variable, lower-cased, classified by shape (changeme/change-me, xxx…, todo/tbd/fixme, <…>, your-…/your_…, …-here/…_here, placeholder/example/dummy/sample, none/null/n/a, replace…, …paste…, …, $…) and reported as NEED 'placeholder value — replace it with the real key (value not shown)'; then the variables are cleared. Nothing prints the value.
evidence: Seeded ~/.config/omniroute/.env with OMNIROUTE_API_KEY= (empty), OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<a fake but real-looking value>, NVIDIA_API_KEY=changeme, BYTEZ_API_KEY=<paste your key here>, and lofty/.env with LOFTY_API_KEY=your-api-key-here. BEFORE: 'ok      NVIDIA_API_KEY           set', 'ok      BYTEZ_API_KEY            set', 'ok      LOFTY_API_KEY            set'. AFTER: NEED 'placeholder value — replace it with the real key (value not shown)' for all three, 'NEED    OMNIROUTE_API_KEY        no value yet', 'ok      OPENROUTER_API_KEY       set'. Grep of every report (four runs) for the seeded strings changeme / LOOKS-REAL / 'paste your key' / your-api-key-here: 0 each — the never-print-a-value guarantee still holds.
fix: DONE. mac-verify.sh check_env_file().

finding: How this was proven, and what was not. Harness under /tmp/h3-test (deleted afterwards): a stub `claude` that records the routing environment it receives (BASE_URL / AUTH_TOKEN set? / MODEL / VANESSA_ROUTE_MODE / VANESSA_PII_OK) and answers per STUB_MODE (healthy JSON, limit JSON with an epoch, limit text, 429 body on stderr, 401 login expiry, broken flag exit 2, arbitrary output with an exit code); a throwaway HOME per test group; port 20128 dead; a python http.server on 127.0.0.1:20999 serving /healthz as the live OmniRoute stand-in; the pre-fix scripts taken from git HEAD; a `stat` shim for the pre-fix runs only (F-H3-07). Lint: bash -n clean on all three scripts; shellcheck 0.11.0 (shellcheck-py in a throwaway venv, deleted) clean at default and `-S style` severity — the only directives are three explicit `disable` comments with reasons (SC2034 for route keys parsed for --status, SC2254/SC2086 for the deliberate glob-pattern matching under `set -f`); a grep for bash-4 constructs (declare -A, mapfile/readarray, ${x^^}/${x,,}, |&, ;;&) finds nothing.
evidence: NOT verified, and stated so the Mac run does not assume it: (1) nothing ran on macOS — the BSD sed/grep/awk/stat/tr/head behaviours were chosen from POSIX-portable forms (`sed -E`, bracket-class case folding, `[|]` instead of `\|`, `stat -f %OLp` fallback, no `readlink -f`) but executed only on GNU userland; (2) the exact wording `claude -p` prints on the Mac for a usage limit — LIMIT_RE is built from the strings in the 2.1.278 binary, and limit-samples.log records which branch fired on each real hit; (3) the real `claude` was never invoked (it would spend the sandbox's credentials), so the probe command's flags are as V2 verified them on 2.1.278, not re-verified here.

area: omniroute failover — new, found while testing
finding: `--force free|local` wrote probed_at=0, so the launcher's very next invocation self-probed the state (older than PROBE_MAX_AGE) and, whenever the subscription was healthy, restored `subscription` before the forced route was ever used. This was pre-existing (claude-auto.sh:61 in the first draft) and would have made the README's own step 5 and the entire PII canary misleading on a healthy subscription: steps expected to exit 75 would have exited 0 on the subscription route. Fixed: --force stamps probed_at=now, so a forced mode holds for a probe interval; the README tells the canary runner to unload the probe LaunchAgent for the duration.
evidence: First gate battery with a healthy stub: every `--force free …` run, before and after, logged 'self-probe rc=0' and executed on 'ROUTE=subscription | PII_OK=1' — the gate was never reached. After the change, the canary scenario on a healthy stub with OmniRoute answering: `--force free -p hello --task lofty-crm-sync` exit 75 (deferred by the gate), `--force free --task weather-news-refresh -p hello --output-format json` and `--force free -p hello --no-pii` reached the stub with 'BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20999 | ROUTE=free-fallback | PII_OK=0', `--force subscription` restored 'ROUTE=subscription | PII_OK=1'.
fix: DONE. claude-auto.sh --force branch; README step 5 note and canary preamble.

finding: The launcher gates on task NAMES. It cannot see prompt text, so an allow-listed task whose prompt drags in a client file is only stopped by the second layer — the existing client-data guard hook whose coverage F-E8-60 says was never verified. evidence: README 'PII canary' step 10; the launcher's log line 'route=free-fallback … pii=0 (task allow-listed by …)' is the point at which the hook is the only remaining control.

finding: (1) claude-auto.sh and probe.sh duplicate their helper functions (filemode, fileowner, hash256, rotate, route_*, envelope, limit_branch, parse_reset_epoch) instead of sharing a lib file: the install contract (README step 3, MAC-SETUP.sh:461-471) copies exactly those two files, and MAC-SETUP.sh is off-limits to me; a comment in each says to keep them in step. (2) On escalation the probe falls the route back to `subscription` rather than only raising the packet: subscription is the one route that cannot leak, and a still-limited subscription is re-detected by the next headless run, so the worst case is an hour-long cycle with the marker in place — never a silent strand. (3) An untrusted route.env is reset to subscription, not treated as an error: refusing to run would hand anyone who can chmod the file a denial-of-service lever, while the reset can only ever pick the safe route. (4) probe.sh keeps a redacted 200-byte sample of an inconclusive probe (its prompt is fixed text) because that sample is what tells Steven why the probe is broken; claude-auto.sh keeps no text at all. (5) `--no-pii` overrides the fail-closed default but never the deny-list — an operator can clear a session, not a client task. (6) Nothing outside integrations/omniroute-failover/, mac-verify.sh, integrations/CONNECTIONS.md:45 and this file was touched; MAC-SETUP.sh, the dashboards, MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md and docs/MASTER-FINDINGS.md were not edited even where they describe the old behaviour (MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md:103 still shows step 5 without --no-pii — it will need the same one-line update when the caller wires the install).
evidence: git status: only the five files listed are modified; docs/findings/findings-H1.json and integrations/cli-anything-harnesses/ appeared during this session from another engineer and were not touched.
fix: For the caller: MAC-INSTALL-comms-data.md:103's post-install check should gain `--no-pii` (or an allow-listed --task) to match README step 5, and MAC-SETUP.sh's needs_steven text could mention free-ok-tasks.txt — both outside my file list.
